summary: Hermann Beythan was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz worked in philosophy and linguistics, studying at Leipzig University (~1832-1834) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1834-1836). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849-1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1875-1888).

Hermann Brockhaus was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel, later holding professorships at the University of Jena (1839) and Leipzig University (~1841-1877).

Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Berlin, under Albrecht Weber, and completed a PhD at Zurich. His posts included Gymnasium Goldingen, University of Oxford, Saint Petersburg State University, and University of Bern (1901-1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1866-1870). He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau (~1868-1904).

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg under August Fick. He served on the faculty at Bryn Mawr College (1885-1907) and held the chair of Germanic Philology at Johns Hopkins University (1907-1928).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1877-1884). He held a post as professor at the University of Giessen (~1904-1922).

Hermann Goetz worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Munich and under mentor Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as curator at the Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery (1939-1953) and director at Heidelberg University (1961-1976).
Hermann Güntert was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1918-1921) and Heidelberg University (~1921-1945).

Hermann Günther Grassmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He held teaching posts at several schools, serving as a professor at the Marienstiftsgymnasium (~1836-1877; 1852).

Hermann Hirt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University, subsequently holding posts at Leipzig University (1891-1912) and as professor at the University of Giessen (1912-1936).

Hermann Hunger is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Heidelberg, and Münster, and later held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, University of Chicago, and University of Vienna (~1978-2007).

Hermann Hupfeld worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1813-1817) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1821-1824), later holding posts at Marburg (~1825-1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843-1866).

Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Berlin and Bonn under Albrecht Weber and Johann Gildemeister. He held professorships at the University of Münster (1876-1885), Kiel University (1885), and the University of Bonn (1889-1922).

Hermann Kulke worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Freiburg, Madras, and Heidelberg under Hermann Goetz. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1967-1988) and as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988-2003).

Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889-1908), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University (1814) and the University of Berlin (1816). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Königsberg (1827-1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834-1839).

Hermann Osthoff studied linguistics and Indology at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn (under Hermann Usener), and Leipzig (under Georg Curtius). He served on the faculty at Leipzig University (~1875-1877) and as Ordinarius at Heidelberg University (1877).

Hermann Sauppe was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann, later holding posts at the University of Zurich, University of Vienna, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and University of Göttingen (1855).

Hermann Usener worked in religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Munich, and Bonn (~1854-1858), later holding posts at the University of Bern (~1861-1863), University of Greifswald (~1863-1866), and University of Bonn (~1866-1905).
